acip: SPYOD BSDUS LAS KYANG, RDO RJE DANG PADMA MNYAM PAR SBYOR BA MED PAR RNAM PAR SHES PA GSUM NYE BAR MTSON PAR MI NUS SO, ,BHA GA DANG LING GA YANG DAG PAR SBYOR BAR MI NUS PA DES NI BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN MI RNYED DO, ,CES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: spyod bsdus las kyang, rdo rje dang padma mnyam par sbyor ba med par rnam par shes pa gsum nye bar mtshon par mi nus so, ,bha ga dang ling ga yang dag par sbyor bar mi nus pa des ni bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin mi rnyed do, ,ces gsungs pa'i phyir
english: And its truth is also demonstrated by the Summary of Activities [a classical tantra on the five stages]: Unless the diamond and the lotus are joined together, there is no way that we can replicate these three states of mind.  No one who is incapable of conjoining the bhaga [woman's sexual organ] and the linga [man's sexual organ] in a perfect way can ever attain the meditative state of great bliss. * * * In the section just preceding, we've had our first mention of the how the five stages of secret practice--and in particular the third stage, that of transcendent mind--relate to the need for partner practice.  Here is just a brief review of the logic of the Five Stages in general, to remind us of just what "transcendent mind" involves.  The selection is taken from the sixth course of the Tantric Series, where we read through the entire text of a famed overview of the secret teachings popularly known as A Presentation of the Levels and Paths of the Secret Word, a text whose formal title is The Illumination of the Scriptures of the Secret Lineage: A Presentation of the Levels and Paths of the Four Groups of Teachings of the Great Secret (ACIP digital text S00196, ff. 15b-16a).  This was composed by the great Mongol savant Chuje Ngawang Pelden (b. 1797).
